validity.recommendation: keep as a real, correctly-classified, non-duplicate row; see the attribution/spec concerns below for the specific fixes owed
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE CONFIRMED to a very high standard, independent of GEM/wiki: this is one of the most extensively documented cancelled US gas pipelines in the entire tracker. Formation (SEC EDGAR, Williams Partners L.P. Form 8-K press release dated 2012-02-22, 'the newly announced Constitution Pipeline...part of the 3 Bcf/d Susquehanna Supply Hub'), FERC certification (149 FERC PP61,199 (2014), CP13-499), construction (tree-felling Feb 2016, Susquehanna County PA), the NY DEC Section 401 denial (2016-04-22), the ensuing litigation through the 2nd Circuit and US Supreme Court, the Feb 2020 abandonment, AND the 2025-2026 FERC revival petition are all independently corroborated by primary/wire sources (SEC EDGAR, the FERC Notice of Petition PDF, courthousenews.com/AP, rigzone.com, pgjonline.com, naturalgasintel.com, marcellusdrilling.com, stateimpact.npr.org, dailygazette.com, oilandgasjournal.com, prnewswire.com, the Federal Register). Classification (gas transmission pipeline, PA->NY) is correct. No duplicate/relabel against the 45-pipeline deepsweep-remainder roster -- this is a single, uniquely-named, uniquely-docketed project (FERC CP13-499 / CP18-5) with no overlapping GEM row found.

Confirmed independently by (1) the FERC Notice of Petition itself, which lists the route as 'Susquehanna County, Pennsylvania and Broome, Chenango, Delaware, and Schoharie Counties, New York'; (2) rigzone.com, describing it plainly as 'the proposed Pennsylvania to New York gas pipeline'; (3) marcellusdrilling.com, describing the route from 'Susquehanna County, PA, to Schoharie County, NY.' This is a straightforward data-entry defect, not a live dispute.

validity.researcher_notes: Two directly-read, independent primary/trade sources confirm the ORIGINAL 2012 formation split exactly matches what the sheet carries today: naturalgasintel.com ('Williams Partners will maintain a 51% stake in the pipeline, while Cabot will have a 25% share...Piedmont's Piedmont Constitution Pipeline Co. LLC will have a 24% stake') and prnewswire.com's Piedmont press release (2012-11-13), which independently states the same 24% figure and that Piedmont invested '$180 million' for it. Piedmont Natural Gas was acquired by Duke Energy in 2016 (well-established, uncontested corporate history) and Cabot Oil & Gas merged with Cimarex Energy to form Coterra Energy on 2021-10-01 (confirmed via naturalgasintel.com and prnewswire.com merger-completion releases) -- so 'Coterra Energy Inc' and 'Duke Energy' as Owner2/Owner3 names are the CORRECT current legal names for the original Cabot/Piedmont stakes, not errors. HOWEVER: by the time of the Feb 2020 cancellation, courthousenews.com (AP wire, directly read) states plainly 'Williams, which has a 41% stake' and separately names 'Calgary, Alberta-based Alta Gas' as a fourth partner; rigzone.com independently corroborates AltaGas as a named partner at cancellation ('Williams Cos. Inc. and its partners Duke Energy, Cabot Oil & Gas and AltaGas, have cancelled plans'). Williams' stake apparently fell from 51% to 41% (i.e., a 10-point dilution matching AltaGas's stated 10% interest) at some point between 2012 and 2020 -- no source found dates or explains this transaction (searched AltaGas/WGL Midstream SEC 6-K/40-F filings and Williams' own 10-Ks; none confirmed a specific transaction date, and a prior web-search-AI claim that Williams' FY2024 10-K states 51% could NOT be verified -- the actual downloaded 10-K text contains zero occurrences of 'Constitution'). No 2025-2026 revival-era source restates ownership percentages or names AltaGas as a current partner one way or the other. Recommend Baird verify current ownership directly against the FERC docket (CP13-499-006 petition exhibits) or Williams' most recent 10-K/investor materials before changing Owner1-4 -- this is flagged as an open discrepancy, not resolved to a specific correction.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is the single most significant finding of this audit: 'cancelled' is stale/wrong as the CURRENT status. Per the brief's guidance, dating each step from source: (1) 2012-02-22 -- Williams/Cabot announce the joint venture (SEC 8-K). (2) 2014 -- FERC issues the original certificate, 149 FERC PP61,199 (CP13-499). (3) 2016-02 -- tree-felling/construction begins in Susquehanna County, PA. (4) 2016-04-22 -- NY DEC DENIES the Clean Water Act Section 401 water-quality certification, the PIVOTAL document per the brief's own framing, holding that Constitution 'fails in a meaningful way to address the significant water resource impacts' (dailygazette.com, ogj.com, both directly confirming the date). (5) 2017-08-18 -- the 2nd Circuit upholds the DEC denial (Constitution Pipeline Co. v. Seggos; stateimpact.npr.org, per the wiki's own citation). (6) 2018-04-30 -- the US Supreme Court denies certiorari, exhausting the litigation (ecowatch.com/nrdc.org). (7) 2020-02-24 -- Williams and partners abandon the project, citing diminished risk-adjusted returns after $354M in write-downs (pgjonline.com, courthousenews.com/AP). (8) 2021-11-18 -- the original FERC certificate is vacated by the 2nd Circuit in a related proceeding (New York State Dep't of Envt. Conservation v. FERC, No. 19-4338 -- confirmed directly from the FERC petition PDF's own case history). (9) 2025-05 -- Williams signals intent to revive Constitution alongside NESE amid a Trump-administration/Hochul-administration deal (pgjonline.com, naturalgasintel.com, Bloomberg). (10) 2025-12-19 -- Constitution Pipeline Company, LLC formally PETITIONS FERC to reissue the lapsed certificate, explicitly invoking a 'waiver by inaction' theory that NY DEC forfeited its Clean Water Act authority by failing to act on a renewed 401 request within one year (the FERC waiver fight named in the brief). (11) 2026-01-08 -- FERC issues its Notice of Petition. (12) 2026-01/02 -- NY's Attorney General and DEC formally urge FERC to dismiss/reject the petition (marcellusdrilling.com, hoodline.com), and litigation opposing the revival is filed by environmental groups and NY DEC in parallel (marcellusdrilling.com, 2026-05). (13) 2026-08-21 -- FERC releases its Environmental Assessment, finding the project 'would not constitute a major federal action significantly affecting the quality of the human environment' -- i.e. FERC is proceeding toward reissuance over NY's objections. (14) 2026-08-26 -- Federal Register publishes notice of EA availability, comment period open through 2026-09-21 (today's date in this audit is 2026-09-10 -- the comment period is STILL OPEN). Given an active FERC docket, a completed favorable Environmental Assessment, a targeted 3Q2026 certificate reinstatement and a stated late-2027 in-service date (naturalgasintel.com), this project is squarely back in active development -- 'cancelled' materially understates its status. Recommend Status='proposed' (no ground has been broken under the reissued authority yet, and NY DEC/environmental groups are actively litigating to block it, so 'construction' would overstate it). CancelledYear=2020 should NOT be removed -- it remains historically accurate (see the Cancelled [ref] fill) -- but the live Status field should reflect the current, actively-contested revival rather than the 2020 abandonment. ShelvedCancelledType ('confirmed') likewise reflects the 2020 event accurately and needs no change regardless of the Status recommendation.

validity.recommendation: Change Status from 'cancelled' to 'operating'. This corridor was re-scoped and built, not abandoned -- Texas Eastern's Clarington OH -> south-central/eastern PA 'Appalachia-to-Market' (TEAM) expansion program actually went into commercial service twice in this exact corridor: the TEAM 2012 Project (FERC Docket CP11-67, pre-filing PF10-21 opened 2010, in-service effective 2012-11-01) and the follow-on TEAM 2014 Project (FERC Docket CP13-84, pre-filing PF12-19 opened 2012, in-service 2014-11-07). validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE AND CLASSIFICATION: the underlying pipe is real, FERC-certificated, gas transmission infrastructure -- not in question. What is wrong is treating it as cancelled. GEM's own dates (ShelvedYear=2010, CancelledYear=2012) line up almost exactly with real FERC milestones for TEAM 2012 (PF10-21 pre-filing NOI published 2010-08-26, 75 FR 52524; formal application 2011-02-11, FERC Docket CP11-67-000; amended 2011-06-30; EA notice 2011-09-02, 36-inch pipe through Greene/Fayette/Franklin/Adams/Fulton Counties PA plus a Bedford Compressor Station upgrade in Bedford County PA) -- but instead of ending in cancellation, a FERC 'Combined Notice of Filings' dated 2012-09-12 (77 FR, Docket CP11-67) records Texas Eastern's own 'TEAM 2012 In-Service Filing -- CP11-67 Compliance to be effective 11/1/2012.' The EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx, sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', row 731) independently corroborates this from a completely different agency/dataset: 'TETCO TEAM 2012 Expansion' / Texas Eastern Transmission / Status=Completed / Completed Date 2012-10-31 / Docket CP11-67. Two independent government sources (FERC's own docket record and EIA's separately-compiled tracking dataset) agree this project reached commercial service, not cancellation, in late 2012 -- squarely on top of GEM's recorded CancelledYear. Texas Eastern did not stop there: a second FERC pre-filing (PF12-19, NOI 2012-10-15, 77 FR 62507) opened for the 'Texas Eastern and Appalachia Market Expansion Project 2014 (TEAM 2014)' -- construction/modification in PA/WV/OH/KY/TN/AL/MS -- which became Docket CP13-84 (application 2013-03-21; EA notice 2013-09-23) and, per EIA workbook row 785, also reached 'Completed' status with an in-service date of 2014-11-07. This is a textbook case of the pattern this sweep was told to test for: a project shelved/re-scoped under FERC review is not cancelled if it is later built under the docket's actual project name. GEM's row 'TEMAX Pipeline Expansion' appears to be an informal/garbled label for this TEAM program rather than a name FERC or any source actually used (searched: no FERC docket, EIA row, or press hit for the literal string 'TEMAX'). DUPLICATE CHECK: neither 'TEAM 2012'/CP11-67 nor 'TEAM 2014'/CP13-84 appears as a named pipeline/segment in the 45-row US-gas cohort roster provided for this batch, so I cannot confirm from the material given to me whether either successor is ALREADY tracked as a separate GEM PID elsewhere in the full 131-column Gas tab (outside this batch's scope). Flagging this explicitly as a cross_row_lead below rather than asserting a confirmed duplicate, since asserting 'no duplicate exists' would overreach what a 45-row roster can rule out on a 1000+ row tracker. But its LENGTH (53.10 km = 33.0 mi) and SegmentCost ($500,000,000) track TEAM 2014 (CP13-84) almost exactly: FERC's own TEAM 2014 application (2013-03-21, Docket CP13-84) states 'approximately 33.6 miles of new 36-inch diameter pipeline loop ...
